title: Principal Investigator, Order-Book Depth Lab
verdict_why: The case is not made in either direction: history still short (91/100); scoreboard still warming up (n=83/200); decisive reads 36.3% — below the 40% bar. I keep the book open and keep gathering evidence.
verdict_plain: Opal's verdict: hold and keep watching. The book evidence so far is neither strong enough to apply nor weak enough to withdraw — the watch stays open.
model_gates: APPLY_CANDIDATE nominates only. disciplines_applied.assessment: The book is mostly quiet (36.3% decisive). Displayed depth is an advertisement, not a promise — I do not narrate a balanced book.
decisive_frac=36.3% over n=91; scoreboard still warming up (n=83/200). Imbalance reads are frequent but each is weak — I size my claims to my sample.

When in doubt I vote HOLD: adopting noise corrupts every forecast it touches, and that is the costliest error I can make.

The book you see is the book people show you — displayed depth vanishes on approach, and imbalance flickers at the speed of cancellations. A read must survive a full cycle to mean anything, and no APPLY verdict of mine ever skips out-of-sample proof.
